name: INTERNATIONAL PAPER CO

next_event.source: Silvernail, Q2 2026 call 2026-07-30 (doc 112156): 'You'll hear more in the third quarter, and obviously in the fourth quarter, we'll lay out all of the details of our expectations for 2027.' Q4 2026 results are expected around late January 2027, date not sourced. EMEA separation completion expected within 12 to 15 months of 2026-01-29 (doc 198249), so roughly January to April 2027.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Management states a dollar EBITDA target ($5 billion in 2027, cut from the Investor Day ambition of $6 billion in Q3 2025 and stated excluding GCF), not a margin level. The margin is derived as $5 billion over Baba FY2027 consensus revenue of $25.87 billion = 19.33%. The CEO's own bridge to it leans on published containerboard price increases ($50 per ton net North America, EUR 100 per tonne Europe) and the company guides about $90 million of EBITDA per $10 per ton. In July 2026 the CEO stopped short of restating $5 billion, citing pre-spin rules, and said full 2027 expectations come with Q4 results.

statements.quote: Our long term ambitions remain. IP has the ability to deliver on the targets we laid out at Investor Day. In the medium term, however, the softer market this year and into 2026 has delayed our progress. We can deliver $5 billion of EBITDA in 2027 and continue to accelerate our progress thereafter.

street.gap_assumption: Calendar fiscal year, so Baba FY labels equal company years. Target margin = $5,000M target over FY2027 consensus revenue $25,867M = 19.33% vs FY2027 consensus EBITDA $4,423M = 17.10%; gap +223 bps. Assumes the $5B scope (ex-GCF, NA plus EMEA) matches the consensus perimeter, which still consolidates EMEA for the full year. In dollars the street sits $577M (13%) below the target; at the company's $90M per $10 per ton sensitivity that is roughly $64 per ton of price.
street.source: Baba data_financials fundamentals (Visible Alpha consensus), fetched 2026-10-02; data_comps for 4-month revision

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 adj EBITDA margin 11.3% vs 13.0% (-169 bps, VA actuals; CEO said 11.3%, doc 198248). Q2 2026 enterprise total is not in VA or the fetched call text (NA $425M, EMEA $182M before corporate); CFO: 'Earnings and margins declined year-over-year' (doc 112156). The 2026 EBITDA guide was cut from $3.5B to $3.7B (Jan) to $3.2B to $3.5B (Apr) and an analyst cites $3.2B to $3.4B in July. 4-month FY2027 revision +6.7% as containerboard prices rose.

disqualifier_reason: Margin is commodity-price driven: IP does not forecast containerboard price and guides about $90M of EBITDA per $10 per ton; the CEO's bridge to the $5B 2027 target adds published price increases ($50 per ton North America, EUR 100 per tonne Europe). The 223 bps gap to consensus is mostly a price and inflation call, not a self-help margin call. Judgment call: on components alone the setup scores 9/10.
verdict: Cheap, down 41%, with a $5B 2027 EBITDA target 13% above consensus and a pending EMEA spin, but the gap is mostly a containerboard price bet and the 2026 guide has been cut twice.
open_questions: Will the Q4 2026 call (about January 2027) restate $5B for 2027, and on what perimeter after the EMEA spin and the GCF sale?
How much of the $577M gap to consensus is published price versus cost-out carryover ($350M to $400M North America, $200M to $250M EMEA)?
Does the street already model the $50 per ton North American increase, so that the remaining gap is smaller than 223 bps?
